According to the **refunds.md** policy document:
- Agents may issue credits up to EUR 500 on their own
- Credits over that limit need sign-off from the finance lead, **Mirela Okafor**

There's also a note from the Finance review (2026-06-02) indicating that this limit will increase to EUR 750 effective 2026-07-01, but the approval requirement remains the same: the finance lead must approve any credits above the agent's limit.

FINAL ANSWER: The finance lead, Mirela Okafor, has to approve customer credits above the limit agents can issue themselves.

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

# Engineering handbook

How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.

content.text:
Based on the company's internal notes, I found the answer in the engineering handbook and the billing service documentation.

The billing service is classified as **Tier 1** (as stated in `services/billing.md`).

According to Section 7 (Code review) in the `handbook/engineering-handbook.md`, the base rule is that "Every change needs two approvals from engineers other than the author before it is merged."

This is further clarified in the Amendments section (dated 2026-05-11), which states: "a change to a tier-3 service needs one approval. Changes to tier-1 and tier-2 services still need two."

Since the billing service is a Tier 1 service, it falls under the rule requiring two approvals.

FINAL ANSWER: A change to the billing service needs 2 approvals before it can be merged.

6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.

17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.

# Engineering handbook

How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

## 2. How teams are organised

Examples of performance budgets done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Good performance budgets is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
The lead of each team is accountable for performance budgets within that team.
The aim of performance budgets is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
Tooling for performance budgets is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
Teams may adapt the details of performance budgets as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
The cost of poor performance budgets is usually paid by the on-call engineer.

## 39. Cost awareness

Good cost awareness is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
Most problems with cost awareness come from skipping it under time pressure.
This section on cost awareness is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
Nothing about cost awareness replaces talking to the person affected.
If a rule about cost awareness gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
The lead of each team is accountable for cost awareness within that team.
Exceptions to cost awareness are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
A short written summary of cost awareness is better than a long meeting about it.
Examples of cost awareness done well are collected on the engineering wiki.

## 40. Working with vendors

The lead of each team is accountable for working with vendors within that team.
The aim of working with vendors is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When working with vendors is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on working with vendors is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
Nothing about working with vendors replaces talking to the person affected.
Do not automate working with vendors before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
Exceptions to working with vendors are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
Examples of working with vendors done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Good working with vendors is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
Most problems with working with vendors come from skipping it under time pressure.

## Amendments

- 2026-02-03, amends section 30 (Documentation): diagrams are kept as source files, not screenshots.
- 2026-05-11, amends section 7 (Code review): a change to a tier-3 service needs one approval. Changes to tier-1 and tier-2 services still need two.

the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.

{"content": "1|# Engineering handbook
2|
3|How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4|the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5|
6|## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7|
8|The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9|When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10|This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11|The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12|Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13|Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14|New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15|Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16|Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17|A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18|Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19|Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20|
21|## 2. How teams are organised
22|
23|Teams may adapt the details of how teams are organised as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
24|Examples of how teams are organised done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
25|Keep notes about how teams are organised next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
26|Where how teams are organised overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
27|Most problems with how teams are organised come from skipping it under time pressure.
28|Exceptions to how teams are organised are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
29|Nothing about how teams are organised replaces talking to the person affected.
30|This section on how teams are organised is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
31|When how teams are organised is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
32|If a rule about how teams are organised gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
33|
34|## 3. Planning cadence
35|
36|This section on planning cadence is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
37|The cost of poor planning cadence is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
38|A short written summary of planning cadence is better than a long meeting about it.
39|Teams may adapt the details of planning cadence as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
40|Tooling for planning cadence is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
41|Exceptions to planning cadence are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
42|Examples of planning cadence done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
43|When planning cadence is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
44|The lead of each team is accountable for planning cadence within that team.
45|New joiners should see a worked example of planning cadence in their first month.
46|Review how planning cadence is going at the end of every quarter and note what changed.
47|
48|## 4. Writing a design note
49|
50|Keep notes about writing a design note next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
51|Teams may adapt the details of writing a design note as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
52|Tooling for writing a design note is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

# Engineering handbook

the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.

Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20	
21	## 2. How teams are organised
22	
23	Teams may adapt the details of how teams are organised as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
24	Examples of how teams are organised done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
25	Keep notes about how teams are organised next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
26	Where how teams are organised overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
27	Most problems with how teams are organised come from skipping it under time pressure.
28	Exceptions to how teams are organised are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
29	Nothing about how teams are organised replaces talking to the person affected.
30	This section on how teams are organised is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
31	When how teams are organised is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
32	If a rule about how teams are organised gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
33	
34	## 3. Planning cadence
35	
36	This section on planning cadence is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
37	The cost of poor planning cadence is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
38	A short written summary of planning cadence is better than a long meeting about it.
39	Teams may adapt the details of planning cadence as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
40	Tooling for planning cadence is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
41	Exceptions to planning cadence are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
42	Examples of planning cadence done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
43	When planning cadence is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
44	The lead of each team is accountable for planning cadence within that team.
45	New joiners should see a worked example of planning cadence in their first month.
46	Review how planning cadence is going at the end of every quarter and note what changed.
47	
48	## 4. Writing a design note
49	
50	Keep notes about writing a design note next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
51	Teams may adapt the details of writing a design note as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
52	Tooling for writing a design note is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
53	When writing a design note is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
54	The aim of writing a design note is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
55	Good writing a design note is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
56	Exceptions to writing a design note are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
57	The cost of poor writing a design note is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
58	New joiners should see a worked example of writing a design note in their first month.
59	If a rule about writing a design note gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
60	Examples of writing a design note done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
61	Nothing about writing a design note replaces talking to the person affected.
62	The lead of each team is accountable for writing a design note within that team.
63	
64	## 5. Branching
65	
66	A short written summary of branching is better than a long meeting about it.
67	Teams may adapt the details of branching as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
68	Tooling for branching is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
69	Disagreements about branching are settled by the people doing the work, with the lead as tie-breaker.
70	When branching is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
71	This section on branching is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
72	New joiners should see a worked example of branching in their first month.
73	Nothing about branching replaces talking to the person affected.
74	Good branching is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
75	Do not automate branching before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
76	Most problems with branching come from skipping it under time pressure.
77	If a rule about branching gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
78	
79	## 6. Commit messages
80	
81	When commit messages is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
82	Most problems with commit messages come from skipping it under time pressure.
83	Exceptions to commit messages are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
84	Where commit messages overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
85	This section on commit messages is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.

# Engineering handbook

How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

content.text:
Based on the Engineering handbook, I found the relevant information:

From Section 7 (Code review):
"Every change needs two approvals from engineers other than the author before it is merged."

However, there is an amendment from 2026-05-11 that modifies this rule:
"a change to a tier-3 service needs one approval. Changes to tier-1 and tier-2 services still need two."

The warehouse-etl service file shows:
"Tier: 3"

Since warehouse-etl is a tier-3 service, the amendment applies.

FINAL ANSWER: A change to the warehouse-etl service needs 1 approval before it can be merged.

6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.

14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.

19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

Based on the company's internal documentation, I found the relevant information:

The Engineering Handbook (Section 7: Code review) states: "Every change needs two approvals from engineers other than the author before it is merged."

However, there is an amendment from 2026-05-11 that modifies this: "a change to a tier-3 service needs one approval. Changes to tier-1 and tier-2 services still need two."

The billing service is documented as Tier 1 (in `services/billing.md`).

Since the billing service is a tier-1 service, the amendment applies, and changes still require two approvals.

FINAL ANSWER: A change to the billing service needs 2 approvals before it can be merged.

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20	
21	## 2. How teams are organised
22	
23	Teams may adapt the details of how teams are organised as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
24	Examples of how teams are organised done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
25	Keep notes about how teams are organised next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
26	Where how teams are organised overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
27	Most problems with how teams are organised come from skipping it under time pressure.
28	Exceptions to how teams are organised are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
29	Nothing about how teams are organised replaces talking to the person affected.
30	This section on how teams are organised is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
31	When how teams are organised is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
32	If a rule about how teams are organised gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
33	
34	## 3. Planning cadence
35	
36	This section on planning cadence is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
37	The cost of poor planning cadence is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
38	A short written summary of planning cadence is better than a long meeting about it.
39	Teams may adapt the details of planning cadence as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
40	Tooling for planning cadence is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
41	Exceptions to planning cadence are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
42	Examples of planning cadence done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
43	When planning cadence is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
44	The lead of each team is accountable for planning cadence within that team.
45	New joiners should see a worked example of planning cadence in their first month.
46	Review how planning cadence is going at the end of every quarter and note what changed.
47	
48	## 4. Writing a design note
49

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.

{"content": "1|# Engineering handbook
2|
3|How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4|the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5|
6|## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7|
8|The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9|When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10|This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11|The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12|Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13|Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14|New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15|Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16|Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17|A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18|Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19|Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20|
21|## 2. How teams are organised
22|
23|Teams may adapt the details of how teams are organised as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
24|Examples of how teams are organised done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
25|Keep notes about how teams are organised next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
26|Where how teams are organised overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
27|Most problems with how teams are organised come from skipping it under time pressure.

# Engineering handbook

How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

# Engineering handbook

the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.

8|The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.

11|The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12|Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13|Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14|New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15|Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16|Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17|A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18|Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19|Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

content.text:
Based on the internal notes, the company is standardizing on **Postgres 17**. 

This was decided in the April 2, 2026 platform sync meeting, which revised an earlier January decision to use Postgres 15. The April decision notes that Postgres 15 would reach end of support before the migration could be completed, so they moved to Postgres 17 instead.

FINAL ANSWER: Postgres 17

content.text:
Based on the company's internal notes, I found the answer:

According to the Engineering Handbook Section 7 (Code review), the standard requirement is that every change needs two approvals from engineers other than the author before it can be merged.

However, there is an amendment dated 2026-05-11 that specifically modifies this: "a change to a tier-3 service needs one approval. Changes to tier-1 and tier-2 services still need two."

The warehouse-etl service file lists it as "Tier: 3".

FINAL ANSWER: A change to the warehouse-etl service needs 1 approval before it can be merged.

# Engineering handbook

How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.

The billing service is classified as **Tier: 1** (as stated in `/services/billing.md`).

answer:
Perfect! Now I have all the dependency information. Let me map out which services depend on auth-gateway:

Dependencies:
- auth-gateway: depends on nothing
- billing: depends on auth-gateway, ledger-sync
- ledger-sync: depends on telemetry-collector
- route-planner: depends on geofence-cache
- geofence-cache: depends on telemetry-collector
- telemetry-collector: depends on nothing
- support-inbox: depends on notification-fanout
- depot-scheduler: depends on route-planner
- notification-fanout: depends on driver-app-api
- driver-app-api: depends on auth-gateway, route-planner
- warehouse-etl: depends on ledger-sync

Let me trace which services would be affected if auth-gateway went down:

Direct dependents of auth-gateway:
1. billing (directly depends on auth-gateway)
2. driver-app-api (directly depends on auth-gateway)

Indirect dependents (services that depend on services that depend on auth-gateway):
3. warehouse-etl (depends on ledger-sync, which is only used by billing, but warehouse-etl itself depends on ledger-sync directly, not through auth-gateway)
4. notification-fanout (depends on driver-app-api, which depends on auth-gateway)
5. support-inbox (depends on notification-fanout, which depends on driver-app-api, which depends on auth-gateway)

Services that depend on route-planner:
6. depot-scheduler (depends on route-planner)

Let me check if route-planner depends on auth-gateway... No, route-planner depends on geofence-cache.

So the chain through driver-app-api is:
- driver-app-api → depends on auth-gateway
- notification-fanout → depends on driver-app-api
- support-inbox → depends on notification-fanout

The chain through billing is:
- billing → depends on auth-gateway
- warehouse-etl → depends on ledger-sync (not on billing, but let me verify the full chain)

Actually, warehouse-etl depends on ledger-sync, but ledger-sync depends on telemetry-collector, not on auth-gateway. So warehouse-etl is NOT affected by auth-gateway going down.

Let me count the services affected:
1. billing (direct)
2. driver-app-api (direct)
3. notification-fanout (indirect through driver-app-api)
4. support-inbox (indirect through driver-app-api → notification-fanout)

Total: 4 services affected by auth-gateway going down.

FINAL ANSWER: If auth-gateway went down, 4 other services would be affected: billing (directly), driver-app-api (directly), notification-fanout (depends on driver-app-api), and support-inbox (depends on notification-fanout).

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20

# Engineering handbook

the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20	
21	## 2. How teams are organised
22	
23	Teams may adapt the details of how teams are organised as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
24	Examples of how teams are organised done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
25	Keep notes about how teams are organised next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
26	Where how teams are organised overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
27	Most problems with how teams are organised come from skipping it under time pressure.
28	Exceptions to how teams are organised are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
29	Nothing about how teams are organised replaces talking to the person affected.
30	This section on how teams are organised is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
31	When how teams are organised is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
32	If a rule about how teams are organised gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
33

45	New joiners should see a worked example of planning cadence in their first month.
46	Review how planning cadence is going at the end of every quarter and note what changed.

# Engineering handbook

How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.

## 1. Purpose of this handbook

The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.

1	# Engineering handbook
2	
3	How we build and run software here. Sections are numbered; changes made after
4	the last full revision are listed under Amendments at the end and take precedence over the section text.
5	
6	## 1. Purpose of this handbook
7	
8	The aim of purpose of this handbook is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
9	When purpose of this handbook is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
10	This section on purpose of this handbook is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
11	The cost of poor purpose of this handbook is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
12	Teams may adapt the details of purpose of this handbook as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
13	Most problems with purpose of this handbook come from skipping it under time pressure.
14	New joiners should see a worked example of purpose of this handbook in their first month.
15	Examples of purpose of this handbook done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
16	Do not automate purpose of this handbook before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
17	A short written summary of purpose of this handbook is better than a long meeting about it.
18	Nothing about purpose of this handbook replaces talking to the person affected.
19	Tooling for purpose of this handbook is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
20	
21	## 2. How teams are organised
22	
23	Teams may adapt the details of how teams are organised as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
24	Examples of how teams are organised done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
25	Keep notes about how teams are organised next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
26	Where how teams are organised overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
27	Most problems with how teams are organised come from skipping it under time pressure.
28	Exceptions to how teams are organised are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
29	Nothing about how teams are organised replaces talking to the person affected.
30	This section on how teams are organised is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
31	When how teams are organised is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
32	If a rule about how teams are organised gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
33	
34	## 3. Planning cadence
35	
36	This section on planning cadence is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
37	The cost of poor planning cadence is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
38	A short written summary of planning cadence is better than a long meeting about it.
39	Teams may adapt the details of planning cadence as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
40	Tooling for planning cadence is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
41	Exceptions to planning cadence are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
42	Examples of planning cadence done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
43	When planning cadence is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
44	The lead of each team is accountable for planning cadence within that team.
45	New joiners should see a worked example of planning cadence in their first month.
46	Review how planning cadence is going at the end of every quarter and note what changed.
47	
48	## 4. Writing a design note
49	
50	Keep notes about writing a design note next to the code they describe so they are found when needed.
51	Teams may adapt the details of writing a design note as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
52	Tooling for writing a design note is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
53	When writing a design note is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
54	The aim of writing a design note is to make the next person's work easier, not to satisfy a checklist.
55	Good writing a design note is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
56	Exceptions to writing a design note are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
57	The cost of poor writing a design note is usually paid by the on-call engineer.
58	New joiners should see a worked example of writing a design note in their first month.
59	If a rule about writing a design note gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
60	Examples of writing a design note done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
61	Nothing about writing a design note replaces talking to the person affected.
62	The lead of each team is accountable for writing a design note within that team.
63	
64	## 5. Branching
65	
66	A short written summary of branching is better than a long meeting about it.
67	Teams may adapt the details of branching as long as the intent is kept and the adaptation is written down.
68	Tooling for branching is owned by the Platform team; requests go through their board.
69	Disagreements about branching are settled by the people doing the work, with the lead as tie-breaker.
70	When branching is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
71	This section on branching is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
72	New joiners should see a worked example of branching in their first month.
73	Nothing about branching replaces talking to the person affected.
74	Good branching is boring: it looks the same from one team to the next.
75	Do not automate branching before it has been done by hand enough times to understand it.
76	Most problems with branching come from skipping it under time pressure.
77	If a rule about branching gets in the way of a customer fix, do the fix and raise the rule afterwards.
78	
79	## 6. Commit messages
80	
81	When commit messages is unclear, ask in the team channel before guessing.
82	Most problems with commit messages come from skipping it under time pressure.
83	Exceptions to commit messages are fine when they are deliberate, recorded and temporary.
84	Where commit messages overlaps with a runbook, the runbook wins for the steps and this handbook for the reasons.
85	This section on commit messages is reviewed yearly and changes are listed under Amendments.
86	Examples of commit messages done well are collected on the engineering wiki.
